composers_checked.name: Guillemain, Louis-Gabriel
composers_checked.note: Gap check against Apple Music and MusicBrainz (no standard work list online): Op. 17 quartets added (not on IMSLP); keys of Op. 17 Nos. 2–3 not found. The other recorded works (sonatas for two violins, violin sonatas Op. 1 and 11, Op. 13 for harpsichord and violin, Op. 18 for violin alone) are duos or solos.

composers_checked.name: Fasch, Johann Friedrich
composers_checked.note: Gap check against MusicBrainz's 295 Fasch works and Apple Music: the other recorded quartets and trios N:B2, N:g1, N:g2, N:d2, N:F1, N:F6 are for oboes and bassoon without strings; N:F2 (Ensemble Marsyas, Graffiti) scoring not confirmed. Epoca Barocca's cpo disc (2007) titles works without FaWV numbers ('Trio in E minor', 'Violin Quartet in F'); not identified.

composers_checked.name: Couperin, François
composers_checked.note: Gap check against the Wikipedia list of compositions: Concerts royaux (1722) and Pièces de violes (1728) are duos; no other chamber work for three or more players.

composers_checked.name: Agrell, Johan
composers_checked.note: Recordings found (Apple Music) are of sinfonias, concertos and harpsichord sonatas only; MusicBrainz has no Agrell works. No chamber work passes the floor.

composers_checked.name: Brescianello, Giuseppe Antonio
composers_checked.note: Gap check: Concerti a tre Nos. 7–12 added (Coviello 2019). The Dresden E-flat 'Concertino' is taken as Concerto No. 4 (same compound first movement). The Dresden B-minor trio (Largo–Presto–Adagio–Presto) is kept apart from Concerto No. 6 (Largo–Allegro–Adagio–Presto) but may be the same work. Op. 1 is for string orchestra.

composers_checked.name: Cervetto, Giacobbe Basevi
composers_checked.note: Op. 1 No. 6: key given as C major (MV Cremona, Tactus) and C minor (Urlicht, L'Appoggiatura single); left out of the title. Other recorded works are cello sonatas (duos).

composers_checked.name: Neruda, Johann Baptist Georg
composers_checked.note: Gap check against Apple Music and MusicBrainz: only the horn (trumpet) and bassoon concertos and the four trio sonatas are recorded.

composers_checked.name: Marcello, Benedetto
composers_checked.note: Gap check: the other chamber works are solo sonatas (Op. 1 cello, Op. 2 recorder) and cantatas; no other work for three or more players found recorded.

note: Sources: Apple Music (iTunes Search API), MusicBrainz, IMSLP api.php, Wikipedia; WebSearch used 3 times. Brescianello: the Dresden trio pages and the Hortus Musicus Concerti a tre overlap; identities inferred from movement plans (see composers_checked); Concerto a tre No. 6 and the Dresden B-minor trio may be one work. Fasch N:G1 and the canon N:F5 are skipped because their only recordings use recorders and bassoon, not strings. Keys not confirmed: Guillemain Op. 17 Nos. 2–3, Cervetto Op. 1 No. 6 (left out of the titles). Couperin's early sonades (La Pucelle, La Visionnaire, L'Astrée, La Convalescente) are folded into the Nations ordres they open, as aka. Neruda's 1764 set is identified with the cpo disc's numbering (its keys differ from the Dresden manuscript set).
